correctness.rationale: The exact coefficient recurrence gives modal localization \(m\le\lambda k(k+1)/2\), including the endpoint \(\lambda=2\) and the zero mode. Hansen/Johnson–Kontoyiannis–Madiman strict log-concavity applies to the uniform jump distribution for \(\lambda>2\), since the condition on total rate and uniform compounding law reduces to this inequality. For \(0<\lambda\le2\), exact integer-coefficient polynomial differences reduce modulo the prime \(1000003\) with degrees preserved. Exhaustive Euclidean gcds across \(109943\) distinct triples find only \((1,3,4)\) for orders four through eight, whose exact common nonzero root is \(\lambda=-6\). The Gauss-lemma lifting argument excludes any unobserved characteristic-zero common factor. The standalone standard-library verifier ran successfully; finite computations cover a logically exhaustive region after the analytic modal bound, not a parameter grid.

originality.rationale: Mane (2023) explicitly leaves existence of three or more global modes open and reports numerical evidence only. Kwon–Philippou (2023) gives partial mode classifications and approximate tables; Georghiou–Philippou–Saghafi (2013) gives mode bounds and uniqueness at integer rates. Unidentified earlier equivalent presentations remain a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The work rigorously closes the first eight orders of an explicitly posed all-parameter global-mode multiplicity problem. It covers the entire continuous intensity range rather than a finite grid, including possible isolated algebraic triple ties, and extends beyond previously rigorously classified low orders. The finite cutoff is motivated by published exploratory plots through order eight and contains \(109943\) verified index triples at low intensities; it is substantive partial progress despite not solving arbitrary order.
